description.narrative:
The activity aims to build awareness and foster synergy between policies and practices for the protection of culture from the effects of disasters trough capacity building, awareness raising and advocacy in the Caribbean SIDS. The activity will help to identify ways in which workflows for risk reduction, emergency preparedness and response for the culture sector can be incorporated within the national/local disaster risk reduction and emergency management.
As the follow-up to the joint UNESCO-CDEMA (Caribbean Disaster Emergency Management Agency) Workshop entitled Disaster Resilience in the Caribbean’s Culture Sector held on 11–12 March 2020 in Bridgetown, Barbados, and the consequent decisions of the CARICOM Regional Culture Committee (RCC/2020/28/6.1.1, RCC/2021/29/6.1.2 and RCC/2023/30/6) to develop the Caribbean Plan of Action for Disaster Resilience and Recovery of the Culture Sector, UNESCO engaged a team of regional experts to work with relevant Ministries and institutions to undertake the stipulated study of CARICOM Member States and Associate Members for further elaboration of the Caribbean Plan of Action for Disaster Resilience and Recovery of the Culture Sector.
The methodology used for this study relied on a desk-based literature review and a mixed-method approach that included both qualitative and quantitative analysis of the data. The desk-based literature review analyzed data and publications from different sources including the United Nations, multilateral institutions, think-tanks, country reports and academia.
To gather the required information to elaborate these national reports, consultants reviewed documents and other resources on the cultural heritage, disaster, and climate change context of each island, examining challenges in relation to the integration of cultural heritage in national disaster planning through the identification of priorities, gaps, challenges, and opportunities.
The regional situational analysis report presents a snapshot of how the culture sector is impacted by natural hazards and climate change across the region, identifying the actions needed to facilitate improved planning, to ensure a resilient sector in the face of increasing threats, and within the context of deficiencies in human and funding resources.
The Caribbean Plan of Action for Disaster Resilience and Recovery of the Culture Sector (2023-2033) constitutes a specific agenda geared towards supporting disaster resilience and recovery in the culture sector, through awareness-building, capacity-building, institutional strengthening, policy and legislation, promoting synergies and best practices across the region, and strengthening coordination between disaster, climate change and culture actors at the national level, and culture NGOS, UNESCO, CARICOM and CDEMA at the regional level.
Further sub-regional consultations and awareness raising with culture, disaster, humanitarian and development agencies on the importance of the integration of culture into the disaster risk preparedness and response strategies and plans are foreseen.
Governance to manage risks for the culture sector of two pilot countries will be strengthened through empowerment of local authorities, communities, DRM and culture sector stakeholders through the integration of culture to appropriate disaster risk management, humanitarian, and emergency preparedness/response mechanisms at the national and site level, as well as through conduction of trainings provided to address disaster related risks to culture. National consultation and training workshops will be guided by existing methodologies and training materials elaborated by UNESCO and ICCROM in this area.
The activity will promote gender equality, in accordance with the international human rights framework, and in ensuring that women and men equally enjoy the right to access, participate and contribute to the activities.
